page_title: How LLMs Work: Pre-Training to Post-Training, Neural Networks, Hallucinations, and Inference

sources.entry: Train a Language Detection AI in 20 minutes

summary.title: How LLMs Work: Pre-Training to Post-Training, Neural Networks, Hallucinations, and Inference
summary.one_liner: You learn how LLMs are pre-trained on web text via next-token prediction, fine-tuned into useful assistants, generate text by sampling, and why they hallucinate and how to reduce it.
takeaways: Pre-training teaches a neural network to predict the next token on massive web text, producing a base model.
Post-training (instruction tuning and domain fine-tuning on labelled examples) turns a base model into a helpful assistant.
Inference samples from a probability distribution over next tokens, so the same input can yield different outputs.
Hallucinations occur because LLMs predict likely text rather than know facts; training to say 'I don't know' and adding web search help reduce them.
Context window contents act as working memory, so adding relevant facts to the prompt improves answers.
summary.summary: This is Part 1 of a deep dive into LLMs, written as a distilled 10-minute read based on the first 1.5 hours of Andrej Karpathy's video. It explains the two main phases: pre-training (data collection from sources like Common Crawl, tokenization, and next-token prediction with backpropagation) and post-training (instruction and domain fine-tuning on labelled datasets). It then covers inference by sampling, why hallucinations happen, and mitigations such as self-interrogation training and web search, ending with a note on the model's lack of true self-knowledge and the use of system prompts. Part 2 is announced to cover reinforcement learning and newer models.
